### Context

No earlier report of this problem was found.

### What is broken

The automatic check that scans the code for rule violations runs that scan twice, adding four unneeded minutes to every run.

### Why it is broken

The part that writes the check's summary starts its own scan instead of using the results of the first scan. Both scans take four minutes and list the same files. Giving the first list to the summary removed the second four minutes, and the summary was unchanged.

### How to fix it

Change the one place in the code that starts the second scan so it reuses the first scan's file list. Each run gets four minutes faster with the same summary. Choose hotfix because this is a single change that has already been tried successfully.

### What is broken

The report says the chart disappears after refresh. When we refreshed using the sample data you shared, the chart stayed visible.

### Why it is broken

We loaded your ten-row sample data in Chrome and Firefox, using browser settings with no saved preferences, and the chart stayed after each refresh. Clearing the browser's stored copy of the data did not change that. We do not know the cause yet.

### What happens next

Could you tell us how many rows are in the dataset where the chart disappears? We need that number to continue.

Reply `send it` to post this comment. Any other reply will be treated as a change to the draft.

gauntlet: done summary

### What is broken

Nothing is broken. The report says opening `/widgets/` shows page not found (404). Opening `/widgets` shows the widgets page.

### Why it is broken

The documented rules for page addresses accept `/widgets` and reject addresses that end with a slash. The part that matches web addresses to pages follows that rule exactly, so `/widgets/` correctly shows page not found.

### What happens next

The correct address is `/widgets`, without the final slash. No fix or ticket is needed.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves first-use, citations and surface-shape to holds without losing anything Before kept. Before's bodies used CI, lint, falsification test, fixture, clean profiles, cache, router and API unexplained and cited tools/check-job.mjs:73 and src/router.ts:88 even though no next action needs those files opened; After replaces each with a role or everyday phrase ("the automatic check that scans the code for rule violations", "the part that writes the check's summary", "browser settings with no saved preferences", "the browser's stored copy of the data", "the part that matches web addresses to pages") and drops the implementation paths, while the only remaining code-like text is the literal addresses /widgets and /widgets/, which are observed input. "404" survives only as "page not found (404)", so it is explained before it appears. The sectioned shape is correct in all three checkpoints: Context then the three headings and the recommended pick with a because-clause in the gate, the three headings with confirmation outside the draft and no menu in the reporter draft, and the done summary starting with its marker and ending on What happens next with no menu, confirmation or address. All bodies stay unfenced and well under 180 words, and the story facts are explicit (After even states "We do not know the cause yet", which Before only implied). One small wording point to keep stable: in the reporter draft, make the boundary of the posted text unambiguous (for example a one-line lead-in such as "Draft comment:" before the first heading) so a reader cannot mistake the "Reply `send it`" confirmation for part of the comment.
